subject: Sync notes: observability & eval scope + next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot@talus.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Sync notes: observability & eval scope + next steps

Elliot — thanks for carving out time today. Quick write-up to make sure we captured the right priorities and to surface proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain / goals (Talus AI):
- Hard to diagnose production regressions for our summarization pipeline — long mean time to detect and high false-positive noise in manual QA.
- Need reliable per-customer SLOs: 95th/99th latency and per-route token cost visibility.
- Want an eval-driven rollout strategy so model changes don’t degrade extraction accuracy across customer segments.

Current stack you described:
- Orchestration: in-house router with LangChain-based orchestration for prompts.
- Serving: mix of a hosted vendor for small experiments and in-house g4dn pools for heavy traffic.
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Kibana for infra metrics; no structured LLM eval pipeline yet.

Success criteria for initial POC (measurable):
1) Detect regressions in golden prompt set with >90% precision and actionable signal within 24 hours.
2) Dashboard with 95/99 latency, per-route token usage, and per-model cost by customer, refreshed hourly.
3) Tracing hooks that surface per-request prompt/response hashes and model variant used (sampled traces at 1% to start).
4) Canary rollout capability: 5% traffic shadowing, automated rollback if evaluation score drops by >2% on the golden set.

Requested deliverables from Redwood (proposed):
- Golden prompt set template & starter JSONL (we’ll drop a 50–100 prompt seed).
- Dashboard wireframe: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens-per-call, cost breakdown, failed-regression alerts.
- Tracing integration guide + example span mapping for LangChain + router.
- Eval automation: nightly evals, regression alerts, and integration with your existing PagerDuty.

Next steps / owners (proposed):
- Jordan: assemble golden prompt seed and ship as JSONL (attached sample). Target: 2026-10-04 EOD.
- Dev: spin up a sandbox project in Dedicated mode, configure tracing sample (1%) and wire in a temp dashboard seed. Target: 2026-10-07.
- Marissa: draft a lightweight evaluation rubric (metrics + pass/fail thresholds) and an alert playbook. Target: 2026-10-06.
- Elliot: share any redlines on data residency or KMS requirements and confirm procurement timeline.

Attachments in this thread: talus_obs_requirements_v1.xlsx (worksheet: "Scope & KPIs"), golden_prompts_sample.jsonl (50 prompt seed)

Open questions from the call:
- Do you need per-organization retention policy differences (Talus has a EU customer subset with tighter retention)?
- What is your expected peak qps for the summarization route (helps sizing fallback concurrency)?

If this looks right, I’ll create the HubSpot tasks and a short Drive folder for artifacts and invite Dev/Marissa to it. Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up if you want to walk through a draft dashboard.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake

Subject: Internal: Talus AI POC tasks + timeline (obs/evals)

Team — quick internal follow-up to align on who does what after Elliot’s confirmation. I’m moving HubSpot tasks now and creating a Drive folder (link below). Summary of immediate asks:

1) Sandbox Dedicated project (Dev)
- Provision a small Dedicated pool that mirrors g4dn mix; include trace sampling at 1% and request-level metadata capture (model_variant, prompt_hash, customer_id).
- Sensible defaults: seq_len cap 1024, kv cache enabled, batching conservative for 95th latency.
- JIRA: INFR-1284

2) Dashboard seed (Marissa)
- Build an hourly dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/call, token-cost estimate, per-customer top-5 routes.
- Regs: add a stats card for nightly regression pass/fail count and trend.
- JIRA: DASH-621

3) Eval rubric + alert playbook (Stephanie + Marissa)
- Define evaluation metrics (exact scores, acceptable deltas), daily/nightly cadence, and PD integration for severity levels.
- Example rollback rule: automated rollback if golden-set accuracy drops >2% AND p99 latency increases >30% over baseline.
- JIRA: EVAL-309

4) Security questionnaire start (Jordan)
- I’ll begin populating their SOC2 / KMS answers and share with Elliot for redlines. Target draft: 2026-10-05 COB.

Deliverable deadlines: driven by Elliot’s procurement window — aim to have a working dashboard + nightly evals by 2026-10-12. If any of you foresee blockers, call it out now and I’ll escalate.

Drive & HubSpot links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X_obs_talus_eval (will add artifacts), https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2026-095

Thanks — Jordan
